newsitem.title: MALTA: Midland Bank opens Malta branch.
newsitem.headline: Midland Bank opens Malta branch.

text.p: United Kingdom-based Midland Bank opened a branch in Malta on Wednesday, becoming the first foreign-owned bank to have a commercial banking licence in recent years.

Keith Whitson, the bank's chief executive, said Midland would offer services including corporate advances, trade finance, foreign exchange, international payment services to the medium and large corporates sector.
Time and savings deposits to the general public would also be offered and Whitson did not rule out a move into full retail banking in the future.
"If we do see the opportunity in the future to expand into the retail market we have a wealth of experience to draw on," he said.
Whitson said Midland was attracted to Malta by the liberalisation of the local banking sector last year.
"Liberalisation has provided opportunities. The market has potential both locally and internationally. We had sound reasons for coming here," he said.
Finance Minister John Dalli said the presence of a British bank strengthened the close ties which the Maltese banking system had with the U.K.
"Maltese law now allows a greater role for an active monetary policy, giving the Central Bank most of the tools it needs to operate in a market oriented way," he said.
